title: Audit forwarding: at-least-once delivery, ordering, and SIEM integration patterns
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Goal: Define and implement a robust audit-forwarding policy for external integrations (SIEMs, webhooks, Splunk, Datadog) that guarantees delivery semantics appropriate for security/audit use cases while remaining operationally observable and cost-controlled.

Scope: outbound audit streams only (not ingestion). Work includes design, schema/versioning guidance, delivery guarantees, retry/backoff model, deduplication strategy, ordering semantics, buffer/DR solutions (DLQ or object-store spillover), and observability (SLOs, metrics, dashboards). Must support tenant-scoped sinks and tenant-level throttling.

Non-goals: building dedicated connectors to every vendor SDK; we will provide patterns, a small set of managed connectors (webhook generic, Splunk HEC, Datadog logs), and extension points for integrations by solutions/success teams.
acceptance_criteria: Confluence design doc covering delivery guarantees, ordering, idempotency tokens, and backpressure strategy is published (link in comments)
Prototype implementation merged behind feature flag for generic webhook + Splunk HEC forwarder (GH PR linked)
E2E test harness that can simulate transient failures, network partitions, and downstream slow consumers; demonstrates at-least-once delivery with observable duplicates and DLQ behavior

Monitoring: dashboards for per-sink success rate, average delivery latency, retry queue depth, DLQ growth, and per-tenant throttling are added to Console; alert rules for >1% failed deliveries over 5m
Rollout plan with canary (5% tenants) and rollback criteria documented
Operational playbook: steps to rehydrate DLQ, inspect idempotency keys, and remediate stuck fanout processes
comments: 2026-03-05 Sofia Chen: Initial ticket created after SOC review flagged inconsistent guarantees for audit forwards. Noted frequent customer questions on duplicate events and ordering.

2026-03-08 Daniel Brooks: Spike completed — implemented basic at-least-once prototype with idempotency token + per-tenant sequence numbers. Results: duplicates observable in 0.7% of retries in synthetic tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3456

2026-03-10 Review feedback from PM (Lina Gomez): Add explicit per-tenant throttling and fail-open vs fail-close guidance for critical vs non-critical sinks. Suggested adding cost model for egress and storage when spilling to object store.

2026-03-12 Design review with Security and Reliability: Agreed on at-least-once for webhooks and Splunk (with idempotency tokens and sequence metadata), and strongly recommended 'ordered best-effort' for multi-fanout paths. Decided to implement optional exactly-once for a small set of enterprise tenants via persistent queue & dedupe store (costly). Meeting notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SEC/pages/987654/Audit+Forwarder+Design

2026-03-14 Engineering update: Implemented exponential backoff + jitter, capped retry window (72h) with swap to S3 DLQ after N attempts, and added per-sink metrics. Preparing canary config. Internal GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3492
notes:
Trade-offs:
- At-least-once is chosen as default because availability and trace completeness for audit data outweigh strict dedup cost.
- Exactly-once via transactional persistent queues + dedupe store is expensive (storage and coordination) and offered only for high-tier enterprise where contractually required.
- Ordering guarantees: best-effort per-tenant ordering will be provided for single-writer producers; cross-shard fanout may see reordering. We will document ordering semantics clearly for customers.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Schema: add envelope metadata (event_id, tenant_id, sequence_number, producer_id, idempotency_token, original_timestamp).
2) Forwarder: generic worker with per-sink queue, retry/backoff, and sink adapters.
3) Persistence: short-term in-memory queue + durable on-disk or Redis for restarts; failover to S3 DLQ after retry window.
4) Observability: emit delivery_attempt, delivery_success, delivery_failure, dlq_enqueue metrics with tenant and sink tags.
5) Ops: provide console UI to replay DLQ entries and per-tenant throttle controls.
implementation_notes:
Key engineering tasks: implement idempotency token plumbing through producer SDKs, add sequence_number guidance to server-side producers, build generic webhook adapter with HMAC signing option, build Splunk HEC adapter with bulk batching, and add tenant-scoped rate limiter.
Open questions:
- How to coordinate dedupe window TTL across restarts? (Redis with TTL vs in-process ephemeral store + periodic GC)
- Default retry cap: 72h vs 24h? Security prefers longer retention for audit compliance.
- Cost threshold for offering exactly-once as a managed feature (pricing implications).
